classification.difficultyReason: Apply supplied empiricalvolume formula usingcirclearea then convertm³ toML.

content.prompt:
The volume of a dam on a farm is estimated using the following formula.
$$\text{Volume (m}^3\text{)}=0.4\times\text{surface area}\times\text{depth}.$$
The factor 0.4 takes into account the slope of the sides of dams. If the shape of the dam surface is a circle of diameter 40 m and the depth is 4 m, calculate the volume of water held in the dam in megalitres. Give the answer correct to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
The surface radius is 20 m, so its area is $400\pi\text{ m}^2$.
$$\begin{aligned}V&=0.4\times400\pi\times4=640\pi\text{ m}^3\\V&=\frac{640\pi}{1000}\text{ ML}\\V&\approx2.01\text{ ML}.\end{aligned}$$
